title: Company's Entire IT Department Now Just One Browser Tab Nobody Will Close
subtitle: Opened 340 days ago and monitoring a system that no longer exists, the tab has survived a merger, two reorgs, and one very cautious external audit.
excerpt: “We brought in an external consultant specifically to assess whether the tab could be closed. His final report was two words: ‘I wouldn’t.’”
author: By Marcus Feld
heroHTML:
DEPT: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

HEADCOUNT: 1 TAB | UPTIME: 340 DAYS

DO NOT CLOSE
bodyHTML:
A mid-sized logistics firm has confirmed that its entire IT department now consists of one browser tab, opened 340 days ago, which nobody has been willing to close since a company-wide email went out titled, in full: "PLEASE DO NOT CLOSE THE TAB."

The tab in question is logged into an internal dashboard that, as far as three separate systems administrators can determine, does absolutely nothing anymore. The service it monitored was decommissioned in a merger fourteen months ago. Nobody has been willing to test the theory that closing it is safe.

"We brought in an external consultant specifically to assess whether the tab could be closed. His final report was two words: 'I wouldn't.'"
— VP of Infrastructure, requesting anonymity "for the tab's sake"

The laptop hosting the tab has since been retired from all other duties. It sits on a shelf in the server closet, plugged into a UPS, with a laminated sign taped above it reading "ASK BEFORE TOUCHING." A rotating on-call schedule exists solely to make sure someone checks on it every morning.

When asked what the dashboard actually displays, the on-call engineer currently responsible described it only as "a number. It's a number and it's been the same number for a year. I don't know what it counts. I check that it's still there and I leave."

The company's official IT budget for next fiscal year lists a single line item: "Tab maintenance — $0. Do not disturb."
